_comment: Canonical v1 workflow definition contract (Epic E80, E80_S01_T01). A workflow is a declarative, linear, validated definition file: builtin ones live in templates/workflows/*.json, project-local ones in project/.workflows/<id>.json (parallel to project/.playbooks/). This file is the single machine-readable source of the format; the validator (E80_S01_T03/T04) reads its per-type rules from here instead of hard-coding them, so a new step type later is a schema edit. -- KEYS: 'schema_version' is the integer format version. 'top_level' = {required, optional, id_pattern}: the keys a definition file may carry and the rule its 'id' must match. 'inputs' = {required, optional, name_pattern}: the shape of one entry of the definition's 'inputs' array (named run parameters). 'step_common' = {required, optional}: keys every step carries whatever its type. 'step_types' maps each of exactly five type names (skill, playbook, confirm, compute, render) to {required, optional, field_types}: the extra keys that type needs beyond step_common, and the JSON kind of each field (string, string_array, string_map). 'outputs' = {entry_required, kind_values, type_registry, name_pattern}: the shape of one declared output {name, kind, type}. 'substitution' = {syntax, pattern, pattern_flavor, namespaces, substitutable_fields, rule}: the reference syntax usable inside step string fields, its regular expression, and the earlier-steps-only rule. 'non_goals_v1' lists capabilities deliberately absent from v1. 'step_id_pattern' under step_common and every 'name_pattern' use the same identifier rule so a dotted reference path is unambiguous. -- OUTPUT TYPES: this file lists NO output type names. An output 'type' is a type name from the registry named by outputs.type_registry (templates/playbook-types.json); the validator resolves it there, so there is no second type system. -- REGULAR EXPRESSIONS are POSIX ERE, not PCRE, because the consuming validator is a shell script (the same convention as templates/playbook-types.json). -- ID RULE: top_level.id_pattern is the slug rule that skills/j-playbook-new/scripts/playbook-new.sh applies to playbook ids (lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens), and the definition's filename without '.json' must equal its id, as for playbooks. -- This file carries no commentary outside '_comment'.

substitution.substitutable_fields: Every string value inside a step except 'id', 'type', 'skill' and 'playbook' (this includes the strings in 'args', 'options', 'prompt', 'command', 'template' and a render step's 'inputs').
substitution.rule: A step may only reference the run inputs declared in the definition's 'inputs' and the declared outputs of steps that appear EARLIER in 'steps'. A reference to the step itself, to a later step, to an undeclared input, or to an output the referenced step does not declare is invalid.
